image_description: A grand, ornate pipe organ situated in a church or cathedral setting. The instrument features a symmetrical facade with multiple tiers of vertical metal pipes of varying heights, creating a stepped silhouette. The central section contains the tallest pipes, flanked by shorter pipe arrays on either side. The casing is elaborately carved wood with gilded details and decorative moldings. Below the main pipe array, there is a console area, though specific keyboards are partially obscured by lighting and distance. Two figures in white robes stand at the base near the console, providing scale.

The connection between the main pipe structure and the lower console/platform is somewhat ambiguous. The structural supports seem to blend into the background rather than having distinct, rigid mechanical connections, though this is subtle.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification of the instrument as a pipe organ and distinguish it from other large musical structures.
To verify the 3D spatial relationship between the multiple layers of pipes and the casing, ensuring no 'melting' or flatness in the complex geometry.
To check if individual pipes maintain distinct boundaries without merging into each other or the background casing, a common failure mode in dense arrays.
To assess the global coherence, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle high-frequency noise or unnatural smoothing across the entire scene.

focus_areas: Symmetry and alignment of pipe rows
Boundary separation between adjacent metal pipes
Structural integrity of the ornate wooden casing
Realism of reflections on metallic surfaces
Clarity and definition of the console area despite occlusion
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the density of the pipes. AI often struggles with repeating vertical elements, causing them to merge or warp. Verify if the 'stepped' silhouette is physically plausible or if some pipes float without support. Also, scrutinize the 'text' on the upper arches for gibberish artifacts.
